concept.name: Value area
concept.definition: In Market Profile, the price range in which approximately 70% of the session's TPOs (or, in volume-based variants, of traded volume) fall, bounded by the value area high (VAH) and value area low (VAL). The 70% convention approximates one standard deviation of a normal distribution and is read as the range where the market accepted price as fair value.
concept.intuition: The value area is where the auction actually did business — the prices both buyers and sellers kept agreeing on all day.
concept.mechanics: Computed by starting at the point of control and expanding outward row by row, adding the larger of the adjacent rows above and below, until about 70% of the session's TPOs (or volume) are enclosed; the top and bottom rows become VAH and VAL.
concept.formula: VA = smallest contiguous price band around the POC containing ≈70% of TPOs/volume (the ≈68–70% figure mirrors ±1 standard deviation of a normal distribution)
concept.failure_modes: The 70% parameter is a statistical analogy, and market distributions are frequently skewed or multi-modal, so the 'value area' of a double-distribution day misrepresents the auction; value areas also shift as sessions develop.
concept.misconceptions: The value area is not a support/resistance box with mechanical bounces, and 70% is convention rather than a measured property of the market — Dalton himself describes it as an organizing convenience.
concept.example: With the POC at 4,520, expanding outward until 70% of the day's TPOs are enclosed yields VAH 4,531 and VAL 4,512; opens inside that band the next day are read as acceptance of the same value.
